topics.title: Things created by Man Primary 5 (Basic 5) - Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES
RELIGION AND NATIONAL VALUES
FIRST TERM
WEEK 4
PRIMARY 5
THEME - GOD WANTS TO SAVE ALL MEN
PREVIOUS LESSON - God’s Creation are for Man’s Interest Primary 5 (Basic 5) - Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD’S CREATIONS ARE FOR MAN’S INTEREST
PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, most of the pupils should have attained the following objectives -
1. list the things created by God.
2. explain what is meant by God creating man, in His own image.
3. identify the significance of creation as a sign of God’s love to man.
4. list things created by man.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Pictures of beautiful things around God created
2. Map of the world
3. Film - the creation
4. GSM phones
5. Baskets, tables, etc.
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
Scheme of Work
9 - Years Basic Education Curriculum
Course Book
All Relevant Material
Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
LESSON 1 - INTRODUCTION
God creates man and wants us to create.
Man has God’s Spirit and some intelligence to work with.
THINGS CREATED BY MAN
1. Baskets
2. Tables
3. Chairs
4. Buildings
5. GSM phones
6. Buildings
7. Cars
8. Electronics
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
1. Revises the previous lesson based on the pupil’s related knowledge or understanding.
Pupil’s Activities - Participate actively in the lesson review.
3. Asks pupils to itemize all the things created by God and man.
4. Leads a discussion on how man created things with what God has created.
Pupil’s Activities - State things created by man.
5. Summarizes the lesson on the board.
Pupil’s Activities - Copy as instructed.
CONCLUSION
- To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
- Next Lesson - God saves Us from Danger (Primary 5)
LESSON EVALUATION
Ask pupils to state 10 things created by man.

topics.title: God Creates and Wants Us to Be Creative: Meaning of Creativity, Things Made by Man, and Creation as a Sign of God’s Love | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 2 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
GOD CREATES AND WANTS US TO BE CREATIVE: MEANING OF CREATIVITY, THINGS MADE BY GOD, AND CREATION AS A SIGN OF GOD’S LOVE
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 2
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Creates: Meaning of Creation, Things Created by God, and the Creation of Man in God’s Own Image | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 1 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD CREATES AND WANTS US TO BE CREATIVE
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Creativity and Things Made by Man
3. God as the Source of Creativity and Creation as a Sign of God’s Love
4. Importance of Creativity
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of creativity.
2. Mention things made by man.
3. Explain how God is the source of human creativity.
4. Explain how creation shows God’s love.
5. State the importance of creativity.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God created the heavens, the earth, human beings and other living and non-living things.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils that God has given human beings the ability to think, create and develop useful things.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2. Pictures of things made by man
3. Charts showing creative activities
4. Flashcards
5. Samples of simple handmade objects
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9-Year Basic Education Curriculum
3. Course Book
4. Holy Bible
5. All Relevant Materials
6. Online Information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
God is the Creator of the heavens, the earth and everything in them. He created human beings in His own image and gave them the ability to think, learn, solve problems and create useful things.
Human beings use their knowledge and skills to make houses, roads, clothes, furniture, tools and machines. These activities show the creative abilities God has given to people.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of creativity, things made by man, how God is the source of human creativity, and how creation shows God’s love.
MEANING OF CREATIVITY
Creativity is the ability to think of new ideas and use knowledge and skills to make or develop something useful.
Examples of creative activities include drawing, painting, writing, designing, building, sewing, cooking and making useful objects.
THINGS MADE BY MAN
Human beings use the abilities God has given them to make many useful things.
Examples include:
- Houses and buildings
- Roads and bridges
- Clothes and shoes
- Furniture
- Cars, buses and bicycles
- Books and writing materials
- Tools and machines
- Computers and mobile phones
- Musical instruments
- Farm tools and equipment
These things are made from materials obtained from God’s creation.
GOD AS THE SOURCE OF CREATIVITY
God is the source of human creativity because He created human beings with intelligence, talents and abilities to think and make things.
Human creativity should be used to:
1. Solve problems.
2. Help other people.
3. Make work easier.
4. Improve our environment.
5. Develop useful products.
6. Glorify God through good works.
CREATION AS A SIGN OF GOD’S LOVE
God’s creation shows His love for human beings because He provided the things needed for life.
For example:
- The sun provides light and warmth.
- Plants provide food and oxygen.
- Water supports life.
- Animals provide food and other useful materials.
- The land provides space for farming and living.
God’s creation reminds us that He cares for humanity and wants us to care for one another and the environment.
IMPORTANCE OF CREATIVITY
Creativity is important because it:
1. Helps us solve problems.
2. Makes work easier.
3. Helps us develop useful things.
4. Encourages learning and innovation.
5. Helps us develop our talents.
6. Helps improve society.
7. Provides opportunities for useful activities.
Lesson: God created human beings with the ability to think and create. We should use our creativity positively to solve problems, help others, care for creation and glorify God.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. What is creativity?
A. The ability to sleep for a long time
B. The ability to think of new ideas and make useful things
C. The ability to destroy things
D. The ability to copy everything
2. Who is the source of human creativity?
A. God
B. Machines
C. Animals
D. Schools
3. Which of these is made by man?
A. Sun
B. River
C. House
D. Tree
4. Why should we use our creativity?
A. To cause problems
B. To destroy the environment
C. To solve problems and help others
D. To waste resources
5. How does creation show God’s love?
A. God provided what human beings need to live
B. God wants people to suffer
C. God created nothing useful
D. God does not care for His creation
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. Creativity is the ability to think of ______ ideas.
7. Human beings use their knowledge and ______ to make useful things.
8. God is the source of human ______.
9. Plants provide food and ______.
10. We should use our creativity to help ______ people.
C. True or False
11. God gave human beings the ability to think and create.
12. Houses and roads are examples of things made by man.
13. Creativity should be used to cause harm to others.
14. God’s creation shows His hatred for humanity.
15. We should use our creativity positively.
D. Matching
16. Creativity - A. Provides light and warmth
17. House - B. Ability to think of new ideas
18. Sun - C. A building made by man
19. Water - D. Supports life
20. God - E. Source of human creativity
ANSWER KEY
1. B 2. A 3. C. 4. C 5. A
6. new 7. skills 8. creativity 9. oxygen 10. other
11. True 12. True 13. False 14. False 15. True
16. Creativity - B. Ability to think of new ideas
17. House - C. A building made by man
18. Sun - A. Provides light and warmth
19. Water - D. Supports life
20. God - E. Source of human creativity
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that creativity is the ability to think of new ideas and use knowledge and skills to make or develop useful things. Human beings make houses, roads, clothes, furniture, tools and machines from materials obtained from God’s creation.
Pupils also learned that God is the source of human creativity because He gave people intelligence, talents and skills. God’s creation shows His love because He provides what human beings need to live. We should use our creativity positively to solve problems, help others, care for the environment and glorify God.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What things can you make with your hands?
- Mention some things made by people.
- Who gave human beings the ability to think and create?
The teacher explains that God created human beings with the ability to think, learn and create useful things.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention things made by people.
Step 2: Meaning of Creativity
The teacher explains that creativity is the ability to think of new ideas and use knowledge and skills to make or develop something useful and gives examples such as drawing, painting, writing, sewing and cooking.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of creativity and mention creative activities they know.
Step 3: Things Made by Man
The teacher explains that human beings use materials from God’s creation and their knowledge and skills to make useful things such as houses, roads, clothes, furniture, vehicles, tools and machines.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention things made by man and identify some materials used to make them.
Step 4: God as the Source of Creativity
The teacher explains that God gave human beings intelligence, talents and abilities that enable them to think and create. Also explains that creativity should be used to solve problems, help others and improve the environment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention creative abilities they have and explain how they can use them positively.
Step 5: Creation as a Sign of God’s Love
The teacher explains that God’s creation shows His love and care for humanity and gives examples of how the sun, plants, water, animals and land benefit human beings.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention things God created that show His love and explain how they benefit from them.
Step 6: Importance of Creativity
The teacher explains that creativity helps us solve problems, makes work easier, develops talents, encourages learning and helps improve society.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the importance of creativity and explain how they can use their talents.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of creativity.
- Group 2: Mention five things made by man.
- Group 3: Mention five ways human creativity can be used positively.
- Group 4: Mention five ways creation shows God’s love.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews the meaning of creativity, things made by man, God as the source of creativity, creation as a sign of God’s love, and the importance of creativity. The teacher also gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson as a quick test, homework, or weekly assessment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
God’s Love Saves Man: Meaning of God’s Love, Ways God Shows His Love, and How God’s Love Saves | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 3 Christian Religious Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. What is creativity?
2. Mention five things made by man.
3. Who is the source of human creativity?
4. Mention four ways creation shows God’s love.
5. State three importance of creativity.

topics.title: God’s Love Saves Man: Meaning of God’s Love, Ways God Shows His Love, and How God’s Love Saves | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 3 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
GOD’S LOVE SAVES MAN: MEANING OF GOD’S LOVE, WAYS GOD SHOWS HIS LOVE AND HOW GOD’S LOVE SAVES
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 3
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Creates and Wants Us to Be Creative: Meaning of Creativity, Things Made by Man, and Creation as a Sign of God’s Love | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 2 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD’S LOVE SAVES MAN
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of God’s Love and Ways God Shows His Love
3. How God’s Love Saves Man and Examples of God’s Saving Love
4. Importance of God’s Love
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of God’s love.
2. Mention ways God shows His love to humanity.
3. Explain how God’s love saves man.
4. Give examples of God’s saving love.
5. State the importance of God’s love.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God created human beings and gave them the ability to think and create useful things.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching them that God’s love is shown through His care, protection, provision and salvation.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2. Bible story pictures
3. Charts showing God’s acts of love
4. Flashcards
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9-Year Basic Education Curriculum
3. CRS Course Book
4. Holy Bible
5. Relevant teaching materials
6. Online information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
God loves all human beings because He created them and cares for them. His love is shown through the good things He provides and the help He gives people in times of need.
God’s love is not limited to providing food, shelter and other physical needs. He also guides, protects, forgives and saves people from sin and its consequences.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of God’s love, ways God shows His love, and how His love saves humanity.
MEANING OF GOD’S LOVE
God’s love is His deep care, kindness and concern for human beings. God’s love is unconditional and is shown through His actions towards humanity.
God’s love teaches us that we should also love, care for, forgive and help other people.
WAYS GOD SHOWS HIS LOVE
God shows His love to humanity in many ways:
1. Creation: God created the world and everything people need to live.
2. Provision: He provides food, water, shelter and other necessities of life.
3. Protection: God protects people from danger and helps them in difficult situations.
4. Guidance: He guides people through His Word and teaches them how to live rightly.
5. Forgiveness: God forgives those who sincerely repent of their sins.
6. Answer to prayer: God listens to people’s prayers and responds according to His will.
7. Jesus Christ: God sent Jesus Christ to save humanity from sin.
HOW GOD’S LOVE SAVES MAN
God’s love saves man by providing a way for people to be rescued from sin and restored to a good relationship with Him.
The greatest example is Jesus Christ. According to the Christian faith, God sent Jesus Christ into the world to save humanity from sin. Jesus taught people to repent, love God and love one another.
Through God’s saving love, people are encouraged to:
1. Repent from their sins.
2. Believe in Jesus Christ.
3. Obey God’s teachings.
4. Live righteous lives.
5. Receive God’s forgiveness.
6. Have hope in God.
Bible Reference: John 3:16 teaches that God loved the world and gave His only Son so that those who believe in Him may have eternal life.
EXAMPLES OF GOD’S SAVING LOVE
Some examples of God’s saving love in the Bible include:
1. Noah: God saved Noah and his family from the flood because Noah obeyed Him (Genesis 6-9).
2. The Israelites: God delivered the Israelites from slavery in Egypt and led them towards the Promised Land (Exodus 1-14).
3. Daniel: God protected Daniel when he was thrown into the lions’ den (Daniel 6).
4. Humanity: God sent Jesus Christ to save humanity from sin.
These examples show that God cares for His people and helps those who trust and obey Him.
IMPORTANCE OF GOD’S LOVE
God’s love is important because it:
1. Gives people hope.
2. Provides comfort in difficult times.
3. Encourages people to trust God.
4. Leads people to repentance and forgiveness.
5. Helps people live peacefully with others.
6. Teaches people to love and care for others.
7. Gives believers hope of salvation and eternal life.
Lesson:God loves humanity and shows His love through creation, provision, protection, guidance, forgiveness and salvation through Jesus Christ. We should respond to God’s love by believing in Him, obeying His Word and showing love to others.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. What is God’s love?
A. God’s anger towards people
B. God’s rejection of people
C. God’s punishment of everyone
D. God’s deep care and concern for humanity
2. Which of these is a way God shows His love?
A. Provision
B. Hatred
C. Neglect
D. Cruelty
3. Who did God send to save humanity from sin?
A. Moses
B. David
C. Jesus Christ
D. Daniel
4. How does God’s love save man?
A. By encouraging people to continue in sin
B. By providing salvation from sin through Jesus Christ
C. By making people hate others
D. By preventing people from praying
5. Which Bible character was saved from the lions?
A. Abraham
B. Daniel
C. Noah
D. Joseph
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. God created and ______ human beings.
7. God provides our daily ______.
8. God sent ______ Christ to save humanity from sin.
9. God forgives people who sincerely ______ of their sins.
10. God’s love gives us ______ in difficult times.
C. True or False
11. God loves human beings and cares for them.
12. God shows His love through provision and protection.
13. Jesus Christ was sent to save humanity from sin.
14. God’s love encourages people to love one another.
15. We should show love and kindness to others.
D. Matching
16. Forgiveness - A. Protection from danger
17. Jesus Christ - B. Deep care and concern
18. Protection - C. Supplying what is needed
19. God’s Love - D. Saviour of humanity
20. Provision - E. Pardon for sins
ANSWER KEY
1. D 2. A 3. C. 4. B 5. B
6. loves 7. needs 8. Jesus 9. repent 10. hope
11. True 12. True 13. True 14. True 15. True
16. Forgiveness - E. Pardon for sins
19. Jesus Christ - D. Saviour of humanity
18. Protection - A. Protection from danger
19. God’s Love - B. Deep care and concern
20. Provision - C. Supplying what is needed
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that God’s love means His care and kindness towards all human beings. God shows His love through creation, provision, protection, guidance, forgiveness and answered prayers.
Pupils also learned that God sent Jesus Christ to save people from sin. God’s love gives us hope, comfort and forgiveness. We should show our love for God by obeying His Word and showing love, kindness and forgiveness to others.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What does love mean?
- How do your parents show love to you?
- How does God show His love to us?
The teacher explains that God loves all human beings and cares for us.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention ways their parents and God show love.
Step 2: Meaning of God’s Love
The teacher explains that God’s love means His care, kindness and concern for all human beings. God loves us because He created us and cares for us.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of God’s love in their own words.
Step 3: Ways God Shows His Love
The teacher explains that God shows His love in many ways, such as giving us food and water, protecting us, guiding us, forgiving our sins, answering our prayers and giving us Jesus Christ.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention different ways God shows His love to them and their families.
Step 4: How God’s Love Saves Man
The teacher explains that God sent Jesus Christ to save people from sin. Jesus teaches us to repent, believe in God, love others and do what is right.
The teacher also explains that God’s saving love gives us forgiveness, hope and a good relationship with God.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain how Jesus Christ saves people from sin and mention ways they can respond to God’s love.
Step 5: Examples of God’s Saving Love
The teacher explains how God showed His saving love to people in the Bible, such as Noah, the Israelites and Daniel.
The teacher also explains that God saved Noah and his family from the flood, delivered the Israelites from slavery in Egypt and protected Daniel in the lions’ den.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen to the Bible stories and mention how God helped and saved the people.
Step 6: Importance of God’s Love
The teacher explains that God’s love gives us hope, comfort, forgiveness and salvation. It also teaches us to love, care for and forgive others.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the importance of God’s love and explain how they can show love and kindness to others.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of God’s love.
- Group 2: Mention five ways God shows His love.
- Group 3: Explain how God’s love saves man.
- Group 4: Mention five importance of God’s love.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews the meaning of God’s love, ways God shows His love, how God’s love saves man and the importance of God’s love. The teacher also gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson as a quick test, homework or weekly assessment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
God Saves Us from Danger: How God Delivers Those Who Trust in Him, God’s Ever-Present Deliverance, and Examples of God’s Deliverance | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 4 Christian Religious Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. What is God’s love?
2. Mention five ways God shows His love.
3. Who did God send to save humanity from sin?
4. Mention three examples of God’s saving love in the Bible.
5. State four importance of God’s love.

topics.title: God Supplies Our Needs: How God Provides for Our Needs and Things God Provides for Us | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 5 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
GOD SUPPLIES OUR NEEDS: HOW GOD PROVIDES FOR OUR NEESS AND THINGS GOD PROVIDES FOR US
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 5
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Saves Us from Danger: How God Delivers Those Who Trust in Him, God’s Ever-Present Deliverance, and Examples of God’s Deliverance | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 4 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD SUPPLIES OUR NEEDS
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of God’s Provision and How God Provides for Our Needs
3. Things God Provides for Us
4. Our Responsibilities for God’s Provision
5. Importance of God’s Provision
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain how God provides for our needs.
2. Mention things God provides for us.
3. Explain the importance of God’s provision.
4. State how we should respond to God’s provision.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God protects and delivers His people from danger.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils that God also provides the things people need to live.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2. Pictures of food, water, clothing and shelter
3. Charts showing God’s provision
4. Flashcards
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9-Year Basic Education Curriculum
3. CRS Course Book
4. Holy Bible
5. Relevant teaching materials
6. Online information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Every human being needs certain things to live a healthy and meaningful life. These include food, water, clothing, shelter, good health and other basic needs.
God provides many of these needs through His creation and through the work of people. For example, farmers grow crops, but God provides the land, rain, sunshine and other things needed for farming.
In this lesson, pupils will learn how God provides for our needs and the things God provides for us.
MEANING OF GOD’S PROVISION
God’s provision means the good things God gives or makes available to meet our needs. God cares for His creation and provides what people need to live.
Matthew 6:31-32 teaches that God knows what we need. We should therefore trust Him while also working responsibly.
HOW GOD PROVIDES FOR OUR NEEDS
God provides for our needs in different ways:
1. Through nature: God provides rain, sunshine, air, land, plants and water.
2. Through other people: Parents, guardians, teachers, farmers, doctors and other workers help provide our needs.
3. Through work: God gives people strength, skills and opportunities to work and earn a living.
4. Through answered prayers: We can pray to God for our needs and trust Him to provide according to His will.
5. Through His creation: Animals, plants, land and other natural resources provide useful things for human life.
We should not be lazy because we trust God. We should work hard, use our talents and be responsible.
THINGS GOD PROVIDES FOR US
God provides or makes available many things that support life, including:
- Food
- Water
- Air
- Sunshine
- Rain
- Land
- Plants
- Animals
- Shelter and materials for building
- Strength, wisdom and abilities
God also provides people who care for and help us, such as parents, guardians, teachers and other members of the community.
OUR RESPONSIBILITIES FOR GOD’S PROVISION
Since God provides for us, we should:
1. Thank God for His provision.
2. Use His gifts wisely.
3. Avoid wasting food and other resources.
4. Work hard and use our talents.
5. Share with people who are in need.
6. Take care of the environment.
7. Pray and trust God.
8. Be content with what we have.
IMPORTANCE OF GOD’S PROVISION
God’s provision is important because it:
1. Helps us meet our basic needs.
2. Shows that God cares for us.
3. Gives us strength to live and work.
4. Helps us grow and stay healthy.
5. Gives us reasons to thank God.
6. Teaches us to depend on God.
7. Encourages us to help others.
Lesson: God provides for our needs through His creation, other people, work and other means. We should trust God, work hard, use His gifts wisely and share with others.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. What does God’s provision mean?
A. God refuses to help people
B. God wants people to suffer
C. God gives or makes available what we need
D. God takes everything away
2. Which of these is a basic need?
A. Food
B. Game
C. Television
D. Toy
3. How does God provide rain and sunshine?
A. Through toys
B. Through computers
C. Through cars
D. Through His creation
4. Which person helps provide food through farming?
A. Painter
B. Farmer
C. Driver
D. Tailor
5. What should we do with God’s provision?
A. Use it wisely
B. Hide it from everyone
C. Destroy it
D. Waste it
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. God provides for our ______.
7. Food and water are basic ______.
8. God provides rain and ______.
9. We should ______ God for His provision.
10. We should share with people who are in ______.
C. True or False
11. God cares about our needs.
12. Food and water are basic human needs.
13. We should waste the things God provides.
14. God can provide through other people.
15. We should thank God for His provision.
D. Matching
16. God - A. Helps us breathe
17. Rain - B. Gives us energy
18. Air - C. Needed for drinking and life
19. Food - D. Helps crops grow
20. Water - E. Provider of our needs
ANSWER KEY
1. C 2. A 3. D 4. B 5. A
6. needs 7. needs 8. sunshine 9. thank 10. need
11. True 12. True 13. False 14. True 15. True
16. God - E. Provider of our needs
17. Rain - D. Helps crops grow
18. Air - A. Helps us breathe
19. Food - B. Gives us energy
20. Water - C. Needed for drinking and life
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that God’s provision means the good things God gives or makes available to meet our needs.
God provides for us through His creation, nature, other people, work and answered prayers. He provides things such as food, water, air, rain, sunshine, land, plants and animals.
Pupils also learned that God’s provision shows His love and care for us. We should thank God, work hard, use His gifts wisely, avoid waste, share with people in need and care for the environment.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What things do we need every day?
- Who provides food and water for us?
- How does God provide for us?
The teacher explains that God cares for people and provides many things they need to live.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention things they need every day.
Step 2: Meaning of God’s Provision
The teacher explains that God’s provision means the good things God gives or makes available to meet our needs.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of God’s provision in their own words.
Step 3: How God Provides for Our Needs
The teacher explains that God provides through nature, other people, work, answered prayers and His creation.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways God provides for their needs.
Step 4: Things God Provides for Us
The teacher explains that God provides or makes available food, water, air, sunshine, rain, land, plants, animals and other things that support life.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention things God provides and explain how they are useful.
Step 5: Our Responsibilities for God’s Provision
The teacher explains that we should thank God, use His gifts wisely, avoid waste, work hard, share with others and care for the environment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways they can take care of the things God provides.
Step 6: Importance of God’s Provision
The teacher explains that God’s provision helps us meet our needs, stay healthy, grow, work and live well. It also shows that God cares for us.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state the importance of God’s provision.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of God’s provision.
- Group 2: Mention five things God provides for us.
- Group 3: Mention five ways God provides for our needs.
- Group 4: Mention five ways we should use God’s provision wisely.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews the meaning of God’s provision, how God provides for our needs, things God provides and our responsibilities towards God’s provision. The teacher also gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson as a quick test, homework or weekly assessment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

topics.title: God Wants Us to Work: Meaning and Types of Work, and Reasons Why People Should Work | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 6 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
HOD WANTS US TO WORK: MEANING AND TYPES OF WORK, AND WHY PEOPLE SHOULD WORK
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 6
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Supplies Our Needs: How God Provides for Our Needs and Things God Provides for Us | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 5 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD WANTS US TO WORK
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning and Types of Work
3. Why God Wants Us to Work
4. Reasons Why People Should Work
5. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
6. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of work.
2. Mention different types of work.
3. Explain why God wants us to work.
4. State reasons why people should work.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God provides for our needs through His creation, other people, work and other means.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils that people should also work responsibly and use the abilities God has given them.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2. Pictures of people doing different types of work
3. Charts showing different occupations
4. Flashcards
5. Simple working tools such as a hoe, hammer or sewing materials
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9-Year Basic Education Curriculum
3. CRS Course Book
4. Holy Bible
5. Relevant teaching materials
6. Online information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Work is an important part of human life. People work at home, in schools, farms, offices, markets, hospitals, workshops and many other places.
God wants people to use their abilities and strength to work and do useful things. Work helps people meet their needs and serve others.
In this lesson, pupils will learn the meaning of work, different types of work and reasons why people should work.
MEANING OF WORK
Work is an activity that involves physical or mental effort to do or produce something useful. Work can also be a job or occupation through which a person earns a living.
The Bible teaches that God gave human beings work to do. In Genesis 2:15, God placed Adam in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
Work is therefore not something people should be ashamed of. People should be willing to work honestly and responsibly.
TYPES OF WORK
There are different types of work people do in society. Examples include:
1. Farming: Growing crops and rearing animals.
2. Teaching: Helping people to gain knowledge and skills.
3. Trading: Buying and selling goods and services.
4. Carpentry: Making and repairing wooden items.
5. Sewing: Making clothes and other fabric items.
6. Driving: Transporting people or goods from one place to another.
7. Medicine: Caring for sick and injured people.
8. Engineering: Designing, building and maintaining machines and structures.
9. Catering: Preparing and serving food.
10. Hairdressing: Cutting, styling and caring for people’s hair.
11. Welding: Joining metal parts together.
12. Building: Constructing houses and other structures.
Both physical and mental work are useful. People should respect honest work, whether it is done with the hands or with the mind.
WHY GOD WANTS US TO WORK
God wants us to work because He has given human beings abilities, strength, talents and skills.
Work helps people to:
1. Take care of their needs.
2. Use their talents and abilities.
3. Help other people.
4. Develop useful skills.
5. Contribute to the development of society.
6. Live responsibly.
7. Earn a living honestly.
The Bible teaches that people should not be lazy but should work responsibly. 2 Thessalonians 3:10-13 teaches the importance of responsible work. Genesis 2:15 also shows that work was given to human beings from the beginning.
REASONS WHY PEOPLE SHOULD WORK
People should work for several reasons:
1. To earn a living: Work helps people earn money to meet their needs.
2. To provide for the family: Parents and guardians work to provide food, clothing, shelter and other needs.
3. To use their talents: Work allows people to use and develop their abilities.
4. To help others: Many workers provide useful goods and services to people.
5. To contribute to society: Workers help their communities and the country to develop.
6. To become responsible: Work teaches people discipline and responsibility.
7. To avoid laziness: People should spend their time doing useful activities.
8. To live honestly: Honest work helps people provide for themselves without stealing or depending unnecessarily on others.
We should work honestly, diligently and responsibly. We should also respect people who do different kinds of useful work.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. What is work?
A. An activity involving effort to do something useful
B. Playing games all day
C. Sleeping all day
D. Refusing to do anything
2. Which of these is a type of work?
A. Watching television
B. Sleeping
C. Playing
D. Farming
3. Which person teaches pupils?
A. Farmer
B. Driver
C. Carpenter
D. Teacher
4. Why should people work?
A. To become lazy
B. To earn a living
C. To waste time
D. To avoid helping others
5. Who takes care of sick people?
A. Tailor
B. Doctor
C. Trader
D. Carpenter
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. Work involves physical or ______ effort.
7. A person who grows crops is called a ______.
8. God wants us to work and use our ______.
9. Work helps people to earn a ______.
10. We should work ______ and responsibly.
C. True or False
11. God wants people to work responsibly.
12. Farming is a type of work.
13. People should be lazy because God provides for them.
14. Work can help people meet their needs.
15. We should respect people who do honest work.
D. Matching
16. Farmer - A. Makes clothes
17. Teacher - B. Grows crops
18. Tailor - C. Teaches pupils
19. Carpenter - D. Makes wooden items
20. Doctor - E. Cares for sick people
ANSWER KEY
1. A 2. D 3. D 4. B 5. B
6. mental 7. farmer 8. talents 9. living 10. honestly
11. True 12. True 13. False 14. True 15. True
16. B. Grows crops 17. C. Teaches pupils 18. A. Makes clothes 19. D. Makes wooden items 20. E. Cares for sick people
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that work is an activity that involves physical or mental effort to do something useful. God wants people to work and use the talents, skills and abilities He has given them. There are different types of work such as farming, teaching, trading, carpentry, sewing, driving and medicine.
Pupils also learned that people should work to earn a living, provide for their families, use their talents, help others and contribute to society. We should not be lazy. We should work honestly, diligently and responsibly.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher asks pupils:
- What work do your parents or guardians do?
- What work do people do in your community?
- Why do people work?
The teacher explains that work is important in human life and that God wants people to use their abilities to do useful work.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions and mention different types of work they know.
Step 2: Meaning of Work
The teacher explains that work is an activity that involves physical or mental effort to do or produce something useful. The teacher introduces Genesis 2:15 and explains that God gave Adam work to do in the Garden of Eden.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain the meaning of work in their own words and listen to the Bible passage.
Step 3: Types of Work
The teacher shows pictures of people doing different types of work and explains examples such as farming, teaching, trading, carpentry, sewing, driving, medicine and catering.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify the workers in the pictures and mention different types of work.
Step 4: Why God Wants Us to Work
The teacher explains that God gives people strength, talents and skills to work. The teacher also explains that work helps people meet their needs, use their talents, help others and contribute to society.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways work helps people and explain why God wants people to work.
Step 5: Reasons Why People Should Work
The teacher explains that people work to earn a living, provide for their families, use their talents, help others, become responsible and contribute to society.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state reasons why people should work.
Step 6: Importance of Honest Work
The teacher explains that honest work helps people provide for themselves and others. It also teaches responsibility, discipline and useful skills. The teacher reminds pupils to respect all honest occupations.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention the benefits of honest work and state ways they can develop a good attitude towards work.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of work.
- Group 2: Mention five types of work.
- Group 3: State five reasons why people should work.
- Group 4: Mention five ways pupils can show a good attitude towards work.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews the meaning of work, types of work, why God wants people to work and reasons why people should work. The teacher also gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson as a quick test, homework or weekly assessment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

topics.content:
GOD SHOWS US MERCY: MEANING OF MERCY, GOD’S MERCY ON US, AND THE NEED TO BE MERCIFUL TO OTHER
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 8
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Wants Us to Work: Meaning and Types of Work, and Reasons Why People Should Work | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 6 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD SHOWS US MERCY
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Mercy
3. God’s Mercy on Us
4. Ways God Shows Us Mercy
5. Need to Be Merciful to Others
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of mercy.
2. Explain how God shows mercy to people.
3. Mention reasons why God shows us mercy.
4. State why we should show mercy to others.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God wants people to work honestly and responsibly.
This lesson builds on their previous knowledge by teaching them that God is also merciful and expects people to show mercy to others.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible
2. Pictures showing acts of kindness and forgiveness
3. Charts
4. Flashcards
5. Story illustrations
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9-Year Basic Education Curriculum
3. CRS Course Book
4. Holy Bible
5. Relevant teaching materials
6. Online information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Everyone makes mistakes and may sometimes do things that are wrong. When someone deserves punishment but is treated with kindness or forgiveness, it can be an example of mercy.
God is merciful to human beings. He forgives people when they sincerely repent and turn away from wrongdoing.
God also wants us to show mercy to other people by forgiving, helping and showing kindness to those who need it.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF MERCY
Mercy means showing kindness, forgiveness or compassion to someone who has done wrong or is in need.
Mercy involves not being harsh towards someone who deserves punishment and showing concern for someone who is suffering or in difficulty.
The Bible teaches that God is merciful and compassionate. Psalm 103:8 says that the Lord is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger and rich in love.
GOD’S MERCY ON US
God shows mercy to human beings in many ways. He does not treat us according to our wrong actions when we sincerely repent and seek His forgiveness.
God’s mercy includes:
1. Forgiving our sins: God forgives people who sincerely repent and ask for forgiveness.
2. Giving us another opportunity: God gives people opportunities to correct their mistakes and live better lives.
3. Protecting us: God protects us from dangers and difficulties according to His will.
4. Providing for us: God provides our needs and cares for us.
5. Answering prayers: God listens to our prayers and responds according to His will.
6. Showing patience: God gives people time to repent and change from their wrong ways.
A good example is the story of the Prodigal Son in Luke 15:11-32. The father welcomed his son back after he returned and admitted his wrongdoing. This shows forgiveness, compassion and mercy.
LESSON 2 - WAYS GOD SHOWS US MERCY
God shows us mercy by:
1. Forgiving our sins.
2. Giving us opportunities to change.
3. Protecting us from danger.
4. Providing our needs.
5. Showing patience towards us.
6. Listening to our prayers.
7. Giving us hope and another chance to do what is right.
We should appreciate God’s mercy by obeying His Word and avoiding deliberate wrongdoing.
LESSON 3 - THE NEED TO BE MERCIFUL TO OTHERS
Since God is merciful to us, we should also show mercy to others.
We can show mercy by:
1. Forgiving people who offend us.
2. Helping people who are in need.
3. Showing kindness to people who are suffering.
4. Being patient with others.
5. Avoiding unnecessary punishment or harsh treatment.
6. Helping people who make genuine mistakes.
7. Visiting or comforting people who are sick or troubled.
8. Sharing what we have with people who need help.
Jesus taught His followers to be merciful. In Luke 6:36, He said, “Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful.” Showing mercy promotes peace, love, forgiveness and good relationships among people.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. What is mercy?
A. Refusing to help people
B. Showing hatred
C. Punishing everyone
D. Showing kindness and forgiveness
2. Who is merciful to human beings?
A. Nobody
B. Machines
C. God
D. Animals
3. How does God show mercy to us?
A. By forgiving our sins
B. By refusing to help us
C. By encouraging wrongdoing
D. By teaching us to hate others
4. Which Bible story shows a father’s forgiveness and mercy?
A. Noah and the flood
B. The Prodigal Son
C. David and Goliath
D. Daniel in the lions’ den
5. How can we show mercy to others?
A. By mocking them
B. By hurting them
C. By helping and forgiving them
D. By refusing to help them
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. Mercy means showing kindness, forgiveness and ______.
7. God is ______ to human beings.
8. God forgives people who sincerely ______.
9. The story of the ______ Son teaches us about forgiveness and mercy.
10. We should show ______ to other people.
C. True or False
11. We should refuse to forgive people who offend us.
12. God is merciful to human beings.
13. Mercy involves kindness and forgiveness.
14. The Prodigal Son returned to his father after recognising his wrongdoing.
15. Christians should show mercy to others.
D. Matching
16. Mercy - A. Showing kindness and forgiveness
17. God - B. Merciful and compassionate
18. Prodigal Son - C. Returned to his father
19. Forgiveness - D. Pardon for wrongdoing
20. Helping others - E. Showing mercy
ANSWER KEY
1. D 2. C 3. A 4. B 5. C
6. compassion 7. merciful 8. repent 9. Prodigal 10. mercy
11. False 12. True 13. True 14. True 15. True
12. A - Showing kindness and forgiveness
13. B - Merciful and compassionate
14. C - Returned to his father
15. D - Pardon for wrongdoing
16. E - Showing mercy
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that mercy means showing kindness, forgiveness and compassion to people who are in need or have done wrong. God is merciful to us because He forgives our sins, protects us, provides for us and gives us opportunities to change.
Pupils also learned that God wants us to show mercy to others. We should forgive people, help those in need, show kindness, be patient and avoid treating others harshly. Showing mercy helps us live peacefully with one another.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher tells a short story about a child who made a mistake and was forgiven. The teacher asks:
- What does it mean to forgive someone?
- How do you feel when someone forgives you?
- Should we show mercy to people who make mistakes?
The teacher introduces the lesson by explaining that God is merciful and wants us to show mercy to others.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen to the story, answer the questions and share simple examples of forgiveness.
Step 2: Meaning of Mercy
The teacher explains that mercy means showing kindness, forgiveness and compassion to someone who has done wrong or is in need.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain mercy in their own words and give examples of showing mercy.
Step 3: God’s Mercy on Us
The teacher explains how God shows mercy by forgiving sins, protecting people, providing their needs, answering prayers, showing patience and giving people opportunities to change.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways God shows mercy to them and their families.
Step 4: Examples of God’s Mercy
The teacher tells the story of the Prodigal Son from Luke 15:11-32 and explains how the father welcomed his son after he returned and repented.
The teacher also explains that God’s forgiveness and patience show His mercy.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen to the story and state what they learned about forgiveness and mercy.
Step 5: Need to Be Merciful to Others
The teacher explains that because God is merciful to us, we should show mercy to others by forgiving, helping, sharing, comforting and being patient with them.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways they can show mercy to their parents, siblings, classmates and neighbours.
Step 6: Importance of Showing Mercy
The teacher explains that showing mercy promotes love, forgiveness, peace, kindness and good relationships among people.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils state the importance of showing mercy to others.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of mercy.
- Group 2: Mention five ways God shows mercy to us.
- Group 3: Explain the lesson from the story of the Prodigal Son.
- Group 4: Mention five ways we can show mercy to others.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews the meaning of mercy, God’s mercy on us and the need to be merciful to others. The teacher also gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson as a quick test, homework or weekly assessment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.

topics.title: God Saves: Meaning of Salvation, How God Saves, and How God Saves His People | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 9 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
GOD SAVE: MEANING OF SALVATION, HOW GOD SAVES AND HOW GOD SAVES HIS PEOPLE
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 9
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Shows Us Mercy: Meaning of Mercy, God’s Mercy on Us, and the Need to Be Merciful to Others | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 8 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD SAVES
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. Meaning of Salvation
3. How God Saves
4.How God Saves His People
5. Examples and Importance of God’s Salvation
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain the meaning of salvation.
2. Explain how God saves people.
3. Mention ways God saves His people.
4. Give examples of people God saved in the Bible.
5. State the importance of salvation.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that God is merciful and forgives people who sincerely repent.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils that God also saves people from sin, danger and difficult situations.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible and Story illustrations
2. Pictures showing people being rescued
3. Charts
4. Flashcards
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9-Year Basic Education Curriculum
3. CRS Course Book
4. Holy Bible
5. Relevant teaching materials
6. Online information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Salvation means being rescued or saved from danger, sin or a situation that can cause harm. God is loving and merciful, and He wants people to be saved.
In the Bible, God saved many people from danger and difficult situations. He also sent Jesus Christ to save humanity from sin.
God’s salvation teaches us to trust Him, obey His Word, repent from wrongdoing and live according to His will.
LESSON 1 - MEANING OF SALVATION
Salvation is the act of being saved or rescued from sin, danger, destruction or trouble.
In Christian teaching, salvation especially refers to God’s saving people from sin and bringing them into a right relationship with Him.
Jesus Christ is called the Saviour because God sent Him to save people from their sins. Matthew 1:21 teaches that Jesus would save His people from their sins.
HOW GOD SAVES
God saves people in different ways. He saves us by:
1. Forgiving our sins when we sincerely repent.
2. Sending Jesus Christ to save humanity from sin.
3. Protecting us from danger according to His will.
4. Providing our needs and helping us in times of trouble.
5. Giving us strength and courage during difficult situations.
6. Guiding us to make good and right decisions.
7. Listening to and answering our prayers according to His will.
LESSON 2 - HOW GOD SAVES HIS PEOPLE
God saves His people when they trust and obey Him. He saves them from sin, danger and trouble and guides them according to His will.
People should respond to God’s salvation by:
1. Repenting from sin.
2. Believing in Jesus Christ.
3. Obeying God’s Word.
4. Praying and trusting God.
5. Living a good and holy life.
God saves His people when they trust Him, obey Him and turn away from wrongdoing. Salvation does not mean that a person will never face difficulties. It means that God is able to help, protect and save His people according to His will.
EXAMPLES OF GOD’S SALVATION IN THE BIBLE
1. Noah: God saved Noah and his family from the flood because Noah obeyed God.
2. Israelites: God rescued the Israelites from slavery in Egypt and led them through the Red Sea.
3. Daniel: God protected Daniel when he was thrown into the lions’ den.
4. David: God helped David defeat Goliath.
5. Humanity: God sent Jesus Christ to save people from sin.
LESSON 3 - IMPORTANCE OF SALVATION
Salvation is important because it:
1. Saves people from sin.
2. Brings forgiveness.
3. Gives hope and peace.
4. Helps people have a good relationship with God.
5. Gives strength and courage during difficult times.
6. Encourages people to obey God.
7. Gives believers hope of eternal life.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. What is salvation?
A. Being saved or rescued
B. Punishing people
C. Disobeying God
D. Fighting against others
2. Who is the Saviour of humanity?
A. Moses
B. Jesus Christ
C. Noah
D. David
3. How does God save people from sin?
A. By encouraging sin
B. By teaching hatred
C. By refusing to forgive
D. Through Jesus Christ
4. Who was saved from the flood?
A. Noah
B. Daniel
C. David
D. Moses
5. What should people do to receive God’s salvation?
A. Continue in sin
B. Disobey God’s Word
C. Repent and believe in God
D. Hate other people
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. Salvation means being saved or ______.
7. Jesus Christ is the ______ of humanity.
8. God sent Jesus to save people from ______.
9. God saved ______ and his family from the flood.
10. We should ______ from our sins and turn to God.
C. True or False
11. Salvation means being saved or rescued.
12. Jesus Christ came to save people from sin.
13. God saved Noah from the flood.
14. Daniel was protected by God in the lions’ den.
15. Christians should trust and obey God.
D. Matching
16. Repentance - A. Protected in the lions’ den
17. Salvation - B. Saviour of humanity
18. Jesus Christ - C. Being saved or rescued
19. Noah - D. Saved from the flood
20. Daniel - E. Turning away from sin
ANSWER KEY
1. A 2. B 3. D 4. A 5. C
6. rescued 7. Saviour 8. sìn 9. Noah 10. repent
11. True12. True 13. True 14. True 15. True
16. Repentance - E. Turning away from sin
17. Salvation - C. Being saved or rescued
18. Jesus Christ - B. Saviour of humanity
19. Noah - D. Saved from the flood
20. Daniel - A. Protected in the lions’ den
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that salvation means being saved or rescued from sin, danger, destruction or trouble. God saves people in different ways, including forgiving their sins, protecting them, providing help, giving strength and guiding them. God also sent Jesus Christ to save humanity from sin.
Pupils also learned that God saved people such as Noah, the Israelites, Daniel and David in the Bible. We should respond to God’s salvation by repenting from sin, trusting Jesus Christ, obeying God’s Word and living according to God’s will.
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher tells a short story about a child who was rescued from danger. The teacher asks:
- What does it mean to rescue someone?
- Have you ever seen someone being rescued?
- Who can save us from danger?
- What does it mean to be saved from sin?
The teacher introduces the lesson by explaining that God saves people from sin, danger and trouble.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen to the story, answer the questions and share simple examples of being rescued.
Step 2: Meaning of Salvation
The teacher explains that salvation means being saved or rescued. The teacher explains also that Christian salvation especially means being saved from sin and brought into a right relationship with God.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils explain salvation in their own words and give examples of situations where someone may need to be saved.
Step 3: How God Saves
The teacher explains that God saves people by forgiving sins, sending Jesus Christ, protecting people from danger, providing help, giving strength, guiding people and answering prayers according to His will.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention different ways God saves people and discuss how they can trust God during difficult situations.
Step 4: How God Saves His People
The teacher explains that God saves His people from sin, danger and trouble. The teacher also explains that God sent Jesus Christ to save humanity from sin and guides His people through His Word.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen and state ways God saves His people from sin, danger and trouble.
Step 5: Examples and Importance of God’s Salvation
The teacher tells the stories of Noah, the Israelites, Daniel and David and explains how God saved each of them. The teacher also explains the importance of salvation.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen to the Bible stories and identify what God saved each person from. Pupils also state the importance of salvation.
Step 6: Our Response to God’s Salvation
The teacher explains that people should respond to God’s salvation by repenting from sin, believing in Jesus Christ, obeying God’s Word, praying and living a good life.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways they can respond to God’s salvation and explain why obedience to God is important.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Explain the meaning of salvation.
- Group 2: Mention five ways God saves people.
- Group 3: Mention four people God saved in the Bible and state what happened to them.
- Group 4: Mention five ways people should respond to God’s salvation.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews the meaning of salvation, how God saves and how God saves His people. The teacher also gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson as a quick test, homework or weekly assessment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
God Saves His People: How God Saves His People from Trouble and Examples of How God Uses People to Save Others | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 10 Christian Religious Studies
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. What is salvation?
2. Mention four ways God saves people.
3. How does Jesus Christ save humanity?
4. Mention four people God saved in the Bible.
5. State four ways people should respond to God’s salvation.

topics.title: God Saves His People: How God Saves His People from Trouble and Examples of How God Uses People to Save Others | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 10 Christian Religious Studies
topics.content:
GOD SAVES HIS PEOPLE: HOW GOD SAVES HIS PEOPLE FROM TROUBLE AND EXAMPLES OF HOW GOD USES PEOPLE TO SAVE OTHERS
CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS STUDIES (CRS)
PRIMARY 5 - FIRST TERM - WEEK 10
THEME - NATIONAL RELIGIOUS STUDIES
PREVIOUS LESSON - God Saves: Meaning of Salvation, How God Saves, and How God Saves His People | Primary 5 (Basic 5) First Term Week 9 Christian Religious Studies
TOPIC - GOD SAVES HIS PEOPLE
LEARNING AREA
1. Introduction
2. How God Saves His People from Trouble
3. Ways God Helps His People in Trouble
4. Examples of How God Uses People to Save Others
5. Lessons from God’s Saving Power
6. Weekly Assessment: Test Questions and Answers/Assignment
7. Summary
LEARNING OBJECTIVES
By the end of the lesson, pupils should be able to:
1. Explain how God saves His people from trouble.
2. Mention ways God helps people in difficult situations.
3. Give examples of how God uses people to save others.
4. State lessons from God’s saving power.
5. Explain how they can help people who are in trouble.
ENTRY BEHAVIOUR
Pupils have learned that salvation means being saved or rescued from sin, danger or trouble.
This lesson builds on that knowledge by teaching pupils how God saves His people from trouble and how He can use people to help and save others.
INSTRUCTIONAL MATERIALS
The teacher will teach the lesson with the aid of:
1. Holy Bible and Story illustration
2. Pictures showing people helping others
3. Charts
4. Flashcards
METHOD OF TEACHING
Choose a suitable and appropriate methods for the lessons.
Note - Irrespective of choosing methods of teaching, always introduce an activities that will arouse pupil’s interest or lead them to the lessons.
REFERENCE MATERIALS
1. Scheme of Work
2. 9-Year Basic Education Curriculum
3. CRS Course Book
4. Holy Bible
5. Relevant teaching materials
6. Online information
CONTENT OF THE LESSON
INTRODUCTION
Everyone may experience trouble, danger or difficult situations. During such times, people need help and protection.
God is able to save His people from trouble. He can provide help, give wisdom and strength, protect people from danger and use other people to provide the help they need.
God also expects us to help people who are in trouble. We can become instruments through which God shows His love and saving power to others.
HOW GOD SAVES HIS PEOPLE FROM TROUBLE
God saves His people from trouble in different ways. He can:
1. Protect them from danger.
2. Give them strength and courage.
3. Provide help when they are in need.
4. Give them wisdom to make good decisions.
5. Send people to assist them.
6. Answer their prayers according to His will.
7. Guide them away from harmful situations.
We should trust God and pray to Him when we face trouble. We should also listen to good advice and take responsible steps to stay safe.
WAYS GOD HELPS HIS PEOPLE IN TROUBLE
God can use different means to help His people.
For example, God may use:
1. Parents to protect and care for their children.
2. Teachers to guide and assist pupils.
3. Doctors and nurses to care for sick people.
4. Police officers and other responsible authorities to protect people.
5. Relatives and neighbours to provide help during difficult times.
6. Friends to encourage and support people who are troubled.
Therefore, we should not refuse help when responsible people offer assistance. We should also be ready to help others when we can.
EXAMPLES OF HOW GOD USES PEOPLE TO SAVE OTHERS
1. Moses and the Israelites - God used Moses to lead the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt. Moses obeyed God and helped lead His people to freedom.
2. Esther and the Jews - God used Queen Esther to help save the Jews from a plan to destroy them. Esther showed courage by speaking to the king on behalf of her people.
3. The Good Samaritan - In Luke 10:25-37, a Samaritan helped a man who had been attacked by robbers. He treated his wounds, took care of him and provided for his needs. The story teaches us that we should help people who are in trouble, regardless of their background.
4. Paul and the Shipwrecked People - In Acts 27, Paul encouraged the people on the ship during a dangerous storm. He trusted God and encouraged the people not to give up hope. These examples show that God can use people to protect, encourage, rescue and help others.
LESSONS FROM GOD’S SAVING POWER
We learn that:
1. God cares about His people.
2. We should trust God during difficult situations.
3. God can use people to help others.
4. We should be willing to help people in trouble.
5. We should show courage when helping others.
6. We should pray for people who are facing difficulties.
7. We should obey God and do what is right.
8. Helping others is a way of showing God’s love.
WEEKLY ASSESSMENT: TEST QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS/ASSIGNMENT
A. Multiple Choice Questions
1. What can God do for His people when they are in trouble?
A. Abandon them
B. Increase their problems
C. Protect and help them
D. Encourage them to give up
2. Who did God use to lead the Israelites out of Egypt?
A. Daniel
B. Moses
C. David
D. Solomon
3. Who helped the man who was attacked by robbers?
A. The Good Samaritan
B. Goliath
C. Pharaoh
D. Herod
4. How should we respond when people are in trouble?
A. Ignore them
B. Laugh at them
C. Help them when we can
D. Make their situation worse
5. What can God use people to do?
A. Help and protect others
B. Encourage hatred
C. Cause unnecessary trouble
D. Promote wrongdoing
B. Fill in the Gaps
6. God can save His people from ______.
7. ______ led the Israelites out of Egypt.
8. The Good ______ helped a man who was attacked by robbers.
9. God can use ______ to help people in trouble.
10. We should ______ God during difficult situations.
C. True or False
11. God can use people to help others.
12. We should ignore people who are in trouble.
13. Daniel helped lead the Israelites out of Egypt.
14. The Good Samaritan helped a wounded woman.
15. We should trust God during difficult situations.
D. Matching
16. Moses - A. Helped a wounded man
17. Esther - B. Led the Israelites out of Egypt
18. Good Samaritan - C. Helped save the Jews
19. God - D. Saves and helps His people
20. Helping others - E. Shows God’s love
ANSWER KEY
1. C 2. B 3. A 4. C 5. A
6. trouble 7. Moses 8. Samaritan 9. people 10. trust
11. True 12. False 13. False 14. False 15. True
16. B - Led the Israelites out of Egypt
17. C - Helped save the Jews
18. A - Helped a wounded man
19. D - Saves and helps His people
20. E - Shows God’s love
PRESENTATION
To deliver the lesson, the teacher adopts the following steps:
Step 1: Introduction
The teacher tells a short story about a person who received help during a difficult situation and asks:
- What is trouble?
- What should we do when we are in trouble?
- Who can help us when we are in trouble?
- How can we help someone who is in trouble?
The teacher introduces the lesson by explaining that God saves His people from trouble and can use people to help others.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen to the story, answer the questions and give examples of people helping others.
Step 2: How God Saves His People from Trouble
The teacher explains that God saves His people by protecting them, giving them strength and courage, providing help, giving wisdom and guiding them.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention ways God can help people who are facing trouble.
Step 3: Ways God Helps His People in Trouble
The teacher explains that God can use parents, teachers, doctors, nurses, relatives, neighbours and other responsible people to help those in trouble.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils identify people who help them when they are sick, in danger or facing difficulties.
Step 4: Examples of How God Uses People to Save Others
The teacher explains the stories of Moses, Esther and the Good Samaritan and shows how God used them to help others.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils listen to the stories and state how each person helped others.
Step 5: Lessons from God’s Saving Power
The teacher explains that God cares for His people and can use people as instruments of help. The teacher emphasises the need to trust God, show courage and help people in trouble.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils mention lessons they have learned and explain how they can help others.
Step 6: Our Responsibility to Help Others
The teacher explains that pupils can help others by reporting danger to responsible adults, comforting people, sharing what they have, giving useful assistance and praying for people in trouble.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils give examples of how they can help their parents, classmates, neighbours and other people.
Step 7: Group Activity
The teacher divides pupils into four groups:
- Group 1: Mention five ways God saves His people from trouble.
- Group 2: Explain how Moses helped the Israelites.
- Group 3: Explain how Esther and the Good Samaritan helped others.
- Group 4: Mention five ways pupils can help people in trouble.
The teacher guides the groups and allows each group to present its answers.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils discuss, write and present their answers to the class.
Step 8: Lesson Summary and Evaluation
The teacher reviews how God saves His people from trouble and how God uses people to help others. The teacher also gives pupils a different set of 20 questions to assess their understanding of the lesson as a quick test, homework or weekly assessment.
Pupils’ Activities: Pupils answer the questions individually or in groups and summarise what they have learned.
SUMMARY
Pupils learned that God saves His people from trouble by protecting them, giving them strength and wisdom, providing help, guiding them and using other people to assist them. We should trust God and pray to Him when we face difficult situations.
Pupils also learned that God can use people to help and save others. Moses helped the Israelites, Esther helped save the Jews, and the Good Samaritan helped a wounded man. We should be willing to help people in trouble and show God’s love to them.
CONCLUSION
To conclude the lesson for the week, the teacher revises the entire lesson and links it to the following week’s lesson.
NEXT LESSON
LESSON EVALUATION
Teacher asks pupils,
1. Mention four ways God saves His people from trouble.
2. Who did God use to lead the Israelites out of Egypt?
3. How did the Good Samaritan help the wounded man?
4. Mention three ways God can use people to help others.
5. State four lessons we learn from God’s saving power.
